PCMCI.name: pcmci_paper
PCMCI.description: one linear-Gaussian series per seed, as in Runge et al. (2019), Supplementary Sect. S4.1: every variable depends on its own previous step, d cross-links (one per variable) at lag 1 or 2, no same-step links, coupling 0.2 with a random sign

PCMCI+.name: pcmciplus_paper
PCMCI+.description: one linear-Gaussian series per seed, as in Runge (2020), Sect. 4: strong autocorrelation, 1.5 d cross-links (1.5 per variable), 30% of them within a time step and the rest at lags 1 to 5

LPCMCI.name: lpcmci_paper
LPCMCI.description: one linear-Gaussian series per seed, as in Gerhardus and Runge (2020), Sect. 4: strong autocorrelation, d cross-links, 30% within a time step and the rest at lags 1 to 3, and 30% of the series unobserved

VARMA-LiNGAM.name: varma_lingam_paper
VARMA-LiNGAM.description: one linear series per seed with non-Gaussian noise, as in Hyvarinen et al. (2010), Sect. 5.4: a lower-triangular same-step matrix with 0.8 d links and a lag-1 matrix with 2 d links, weights 0.05 to 0.5 in magnitude, plus one moving-average matrix drawn like the lag-1 one

LongitudinalLiNGAM.name: longitudinal_lingam_paper
LongitudinalLiNGAM.description: M units observed at n time points with non-Gaussian noise, as in Kadowaki et al. (2013): a dense same-step DAG and a dense lag-1 matrix drawn anew at every time point, and a hidden common cause at the first

Granger.name: var2_lagged
Granger.description: one linear-Gaussian VAR(2) series per seed with no same-step links: every variable depends on its own past, each other variable enters each lag with probability 2 / (d - 1), every variable z-scored before the fits

methods.settings: lags 1 to 2, pc_alpha 0.2, alpha_level 0.05, Student-t partial correlation
methods.output: one directed graph per lag 1 to 2
methods.error_metric: lag-resolved SHD: per lag, the links that differ from the true links at that lag (a reversed link counts 2), summed over lags 1 to 2
methods.same_graph_test: equal structure_hash: the same links at every lag
methods.accuracy: F1 of the window causal graph over cross-links, with precision and recall: a link joins two different variables at a lag (oriented by time) or within a time step (counted by adjacency); autodependencies are left out (Assaad et al. 2022, JAIR, Sect. 9.1; Runge et al. 2019, Suppl. S4.2)

methods.settings: lags 0 to 5, pc_alpha 0.01, majority collider rule, Student-t partial correlation
methods.output: a CPDAG of the same-step links and one directed graph for lag 1
methods.error_metric: endpoint SHD against the true graph over lags 0 to 5: two for a missing or extra link, one per wrong end; an unoriented same-step link costs its open end
methods.same_graph_test: equal structure_hash: the same links at every lag with the same marks, conflicts included
methods.accuracy: F1 of the window causal graph over cross-links, with precision and recall: a link joins two different variables at a lag (oriented by time) or within a time step (counted by adjacency); autodependencies are left out (Assaad et al. 2022, JAIR, Sect. 9.1; Runge et al. 2019, Suppl. S4.2)

methods.settings: lags 0 to 3, pc_alpha 0.05, one preliminary round, Student-t partial correlation
methods.output: a time-series PAG over lags 0 to 3: every link with a tail, arrowhead, or circle at each end
methods.error_metric: endpoint SHD against the true PAG over the observed series and lags 0 to 3 (the generating graph with the unobserved series marginalized, Gerhardus and Runge 2020, Sect. 2.3): two for a missing or extra link, one per end that differs, a circle in both counting as a match
methods.same_graph_test: equal structure_hash: the same links at every lag with the same marks at both ends, conflicts included
methods.accuracy: F1 of the links against the true PAG over the observed series and lags 0 to 3, whatever their marks (adjacency_f1), autodependencies included; 30% of the series are unobserved

methods.settings: order (1, 1), no order search, lag blocks pruned by adaptive Lasso; like-for-like environment: Andrey runs with lingam's Python, NumPy, SciPy, and statsmodels
methods.output: weighted same-step, lag-1, and moving-average matrices
methods.error_metric: cross-links that differ from the true ones: missing plus extra, a lagged link counted with its direction and a same-step link by adjacency
methods.same_graph_test: equal structure_hash: the same nonzero weights in every block
methods.accuracy: F1 of the window causal graph over cross-links, with precision and recall: a link joins two different variables at a lag (oriented by time) or within a time step (counted by adjacency); autodependencies are left out (Assaad et al. 2022, JAIR, Sect. 9.1; Runge et al. 2019, Suppl. S4.2)

methods.output: weighted same-step and lag-1 matrices at every time point but the first
methods.error_metric: cross-links that differ from the true ones: missing plus extra, a lagged link counted with its direction and a same-step link by adjacency
methods.same_graph_test: equal structure_hash: the same nonzero weights at every time point
methods.accuracy: F1 of the window causal graph over cross-links, with precision and recall: a link joins two different variables at a lag (oriented by time) or within a time step (counted by adjacency); autodependencies are left out (Assaad et al. 2022, JAIR, Sect. 9.1; Runge et al. 2019, Suppl. S4.2)

methods.output: the lagged edges with nonzero coefficients at lags 1 to 2
methods.error_metric: lagged edges that differ from the true ones: missing plus extra, over lags 1 to 2
methods.same_graph_test: the same lagged edges (nonzero coefficients at the same lags)
methods.accuracy: F1 of the window causal graph over cross-links, with precision and recall: a link joins two different variables at a lag (oriented by time) or within a time step (counted by adjacency); autodependencies are left out (Assaad et al. 2022, JAIR, Sect. 9.1; Runge et al. 2019, Suppl. S4.2)
